label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Hi Mikaela, yep, we started on 21 September after mating had started. Happy to give you the warts and all version, especially after all the help you gave us when Dave did his shoulder.

We’re milking 290, mostly 3-way crossbreds. Still start at 5.15 every morning, then skip Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday arvo milkings. So four once-a-days through the week. The cows took it better than I expected actually. About four days of bellowing at the gate and then they settled into it.

Production-wise, we’re down about 6% on milksolids against the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. Our rep said to expect 8–10%, so it’s been less of a hit than we’d braced for. That’s only a comparison with last year though, not proof that the whole difference is the milking times. And we haven’t done a whole season yet, so I can’t tell you what it’ll look like by March.

Cells did jump. We were around 110,000 and went up to about 180,000 for the first three weeks. Back around 135,000 now. So they didn’t go completely mental but I wouldn’t tell you they stayed put either.

The worst bit was a heifer with mastitis that went bad on a skipped arvo. We didn’t pick her up till the next morning and she lost a quarter. That’s the bit I’d want you to know before trying it. You still have to check cows on the skip days, and be right on top of teat spraying. Missing a milking can’t mean forgetting about them till morning or it’ll bite you. We learnt that the hard way.

On the good side, lame cows are well down. Four on the list now compared with eleven this time last year. Our back paddocks are a 1.8km walk, so fewer trips is a decent saving on their feet. Again, that’s what we’re seeing here, not a promise you’d get the same.

For us the biggest difference has been having some time back. That first skipped Sunday arvo, Dave and I went over to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday afternoon we’d had off in spring in twenty-odd years. Still did the morning milking of course, but being able to go somewhere afterwards was lovely.

Kieran reckons it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October. That says quite a lot! With Tom’s knees the way they are, I reckon those arvos out of the shed could make a real difference, and hopefully help with keeping your young fella too.

Honestly, I wouldn’t go back. The hours alone are worth the 6% to us. But it is still milk we’re not sending, and that heifer wasn’t a small thing. I wouldn’t talk you into it on the strength of our spring and then have you cursing me in March.

Come and grab me at the field day on the 19th. I’ll bring our shed rosters and numbers so you can have a proper look. Or just ring me before then if you want, much easier than texting with these useless thumbs!
